title: Exterminauts Is Like Helldivers 2 Starring Home Depot Dads
description: I'm not sure Exterminauts is different enough from Helldivers 2. Behaviour Interactive, the team most famous for Dead by Daylight, told me during a roundtable discussion with the press that the idea of what has become Exterminauts was swirling around in the studio for a decade, with the game being roughly "half" done when Helldivers 2 launched in February 2024. But if you didn't know that, you'd probably think it was made in reaction to Arrowhead's breakout hit. In Exterminauts, the third-person co-op shooter drops you and two others on a far-off world full of missions to complete, loot to collect, and aliens to explode. Side objectives often tempt you to stray from the golden path in exchange for exciting rewards like weapon buffs and mech suits. And when the job is finished, getting home in one piece means holding out while the exfiltration shuttle comes to you, as turrets and other hazards wipe out the onslaught of monsters--and you too, if you're not careful, since the game allows for friendly fire. It is, in essence, Helldivers 2 with a brighter color palette, a different race of aliens to destroy, and missions with different specifics, but played at a similar cadence. Is such a familiar experience enough on its own to merit players making the time for it? We see copycats often in video games, but Exterminauts felt closer to its inspiration than most others that have chased an already-successful idea with a different wrapper. But one aspect really stood out to me as a clever, unique boon to the game: thematic cohesion. Whereas Helldivers 2 nails its Starship Troopers vibes, everything in Exterminauts feels like a sci-fi version of a weekend project involving Home Depot, with its heroes behaving like do-it-yourself dads (and moms, depending on how you customize your character) who treat wiping out giant aliens like a fixer-upper. Exterminauts intentionally chases this feeling, as I learned in a hands-off presentation before I got to jump in for myself.…

title: GTA 6 Music Festival Announced For Miami With A Stacked Lineup Of Artists
description: Rockstar Games has announced Grand Theft Auto 6: The Festival, a concert coming to the Mana Wynwood in Miami on November 21. The festival features a lineup of artists from the game and the official soundtrack, including Cardi B, Travis Scott, Kodak Black, and Justice. The event is sponsored in part by PlayStation and produced by the team that created the III Points event in Miami. The "one-of-a-kind launch event," as Rockstar calls it, will feature two stages of "non-stop music." GTA 6: The Festival takes place in Miami on November 21. You can't buy tickets. Instead, you need to enter a lottery and hope to be chosen. The lottery is open now and closes tomorrow, November 10, at 4 PM ET. Winners will be drawn the same day, and they can buy tickets on November 11. There is a two-ticket maximum, tickets are non-transferable, and you must be 17 or older to attend. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and the festival celebrates the game's release. Justice, the French electronic music duo, composed the score for GTA 6. The game’s in-game radio stations are filled with big hits from famous bands and artists, and podcasts will also be available to listen to in your earbuds as you commit various crimes across Vice City.

title: "The lesson learned is you can have both": Skyrim lead designer reckons there's merit in Baldur's Gate 3-style tough choices and Bethesda's do-anything approach
description: Whether RPGs are better off prioritising player freedom or endeavouring to have several doors slam shut every time you put another foot forwards in order to encourage multiple runs with different characters is, to put it bluntly, something I reckon will still be a matter of debate in the year 4000. We'll all have evolved in non-corporeal beings floating in a galaxy that's been racked by such change that even the six million copies of The Elder Scrolls 5 we've littered the Earth with will have been swept away into the great recycling bin on the gods' desktop, and there'll still be sniping going on about whether it's ok that Skyrim lets you be a master thiefssassin who leads the companions, knows every spell under the sun, and slapped up a world-eating dragon for fun. For what it's worth, the game's lead designer reckons both games that do and don't let you do that have their merits when executed well. Read more

title: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Breaks Sales Records (For Real-Life Ocarinas)
description: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is a stellar remake of a beloved classic, so it only makes sense that it would have somewhat of a halo effect. And given that it's how a lot of millennials learned what the heck an ocarina even is, it makes sense that it would have an impact on demand for the simple wind instrument. Eric Bernard, manager of Songbird Ocarina, previously explained how accurate the ocarina playing is in the remake. (The answer: very accurate.) So we reached out regarding how the Ocarina remake is impacting his business, and apparently, it's doing very well. Bernard said that online order volume radically increased starting September 8, when Nintendo debuted a Nintendo Direct presentation that showcased the game. And then November 5, the actual release day, was a record-setter for the company. Songbird sells a few different models of the instrument modeled after the iconic blue Ocarina of Time found in the game, and that date marked the most of those models it has ever sold in a single day. Bernard also expounded further on the accuracy of the ocarina playing, now that the game has been released. He noted that the game's audio-detection system doesn't require the songs to be played in the exact key of the original music. So while you could learn from Link's own finger movements, you could also play in any of the other 11 possible key signatures to get the same result. The ocarina is a major plot element in Ocarina of Time, and Nintendo made it the centerpiece of this remake in a few ways. It has an audio-detection mechanism that allows you to hum into the mic to summon songs, and an officially licensed electronic ocarina accessory from Hori lets you emulate the real movements to play.

title: Former PlayStation Boss Thinks Sony Is Solving The Wrong Problem With PS6
description: Sony confirmed last week that development on its "next-generation" PlayStation platform will pick up speed in 2027, but not everyone is convinced the world needs a PS6 right now. In an interview with The Trophy Room, former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden said true innovation would come from finding a way to lower the price of the PS5, allowing more potential buyers to enter the market. "I think we have enough power in the machine. The innovation needs to come not from making PS6 for $1,200, it's to make another PS5 for $300. Now, that would be true innovation," Layden said, while also remarking how the PS5 generation saw price increases over time, not reductions. Compared to previous generations, the PS5 has only gotten more expensive in the six years that it has been on the market, rising from $400 to $600 for the PS5 Digital Edition, while the PS5 with a disc drive has increased from $500 to $650. The PS5 Pro has seen the biggest increase in the few years it has been around, as the beefier machine has jumped from its original price of $700 to $900. Various factors are to blame, but one of the biggest is the global memory shortage that has hit all fields of technology, thanks to AI data centers eating into the world's supply. A PS6 that costs over $1,000 will be out of reach for many consumers, and as Layden believes, it likely won't be as big a graphical leap forward as we've seen in previous PlayStation generations. While the difference in video game graphics between the PS1 and the PS2 was especially noticeable, later consoles have shown diminishing returns, and Layden believes the graphical quality of PS6 games will be even harder to notice. "These are the differences that only dogs can hear," Layden said about the reported increase in teraflops and ray-tracing power the PS6 will supposedly offer. "What the company needs to do is do what it's never done, which is don't iterate the console. Make it smaller, make it cheaper, do all the things you can around that.…

title: GTA 6 Preloading Is Officially Live, Files Mention Multiplayer And PS5 Pro Features
description: At long last, you can now install Grand Theft Auto 6 on your console via preloading, or at least you can if you live in Australia or New Zealand. Preloading begins in all regions at midnight local time, so people in the US are almost there. With preloading now live, people have dug through the files and found things they weren't intended to see. That includes references to things like "join Session," "launch Activity," and "launch Multiplayer Activity." People are taking these to be references to a new form of GTA Online. Rockstar has said GTA 6 is a single-player game, but it’s expected to add some form of online multiplayer at some point. Just because "Multiplayer" was found in the game's files, that doesn't necessarily mean online functionality will be available at launch--it's likely coming sometime later. People have theorized that GTA 6's story and Online could be separate games. That remains to be seen, but those who have the game preloaded have discovered that GTA 6's "Story" is an individual download within the game's files. Whatever the case, experts and insiders believe GTA 6's new online experience will launch at some point in 2027. Additionally, the datamining effort led to some discoveries about what Rockstar might be cooking up in terms of PS5 Pro support. People believe they found references to 120Hz support on PS5 Pro, along with multi-frame super resolution, which is known as PSSR on PS5 Pro. Rockstar has yet to announce any specifics about GTA 6 for PS5 Pro, and the game's trailers so far have been captured on a standard PS5. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. For more, check out the exact worldwide launch times. The game's non-simultaneous launch means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get in. If that has you thinking about booking a flight to New Zealand, here's how to safely pack your PS5 for the flight.

Still, the two investigations are likely to start a bizarre new leg in the alread-messy AI arms race that the US and China have been indulging in for years. Read more

title: Mortal Kombat 2 Is Winning The Race To Become Mortal Kombat 2
description: What's in a name? That's the question that Mortal Kombat studio CCO Ed Boon is asking, as he recently set up a few polls asking for opinions on what the next Mortal Kombat game should be called. According to Boon, three possible names were on the table: Mortal Kombat 12, Mortal Kombat 13, or Mortal Kombat 2. "Footnote: Some people are assuming the title with the most votes will determine where we take the story," Boon wrote online. "That’s not the case. We’ve just had difficulty kounting lately." The current naming convention for Mortal Kombat doesn't make much sense if you've taken a break from the franchise. The series made a successful comeback in 2011 with Mortal Kombat, the ninth installment in the franchise. This was followed by Mortal Kombat X in 2015 and Mortal Kombat 11 in 2019, which brought the original storyline that began in 1992's Mortal Kombat to a close. This was followed by a soft reboot in 2023 with Mortal Kombat 1, which remixed established story beats and put familiar characters in new roles. To make things even more confusing, Mortal Kombat 1 heavily references multiple timelines toward the end of its campaign, drawing in characters from across a Mortal Kombat multiverse for a final showdown against Shang Tsung from the previous timeline. The Khaos Reigns expansion would also touch on these ideas, as the Titan version of Havik sought to merge all timelines into one. Currently, "Mortal Kombat 2" is leading the votes with 45.2% of people polled by Boon favoring that title, at the time of writing. If this becomes the title of the next Mortal Kombat game, it will be the second Mortal Kombat 2, which will probably confuse anyone who hasn't been following along. While it hasn't been officially revealed yet, Boon did confirm that Mortal Kombat developer NetherRealm Studios is "pursuing another Mortal Kombat game," and he added that "other forms of media and whatnot" for the Mortal Kombat franchise are in development. That was back in May, and since…

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Under Investigation Following Affair With Suspected Chinese Spy
description: Nvidia has announced that it has opened an official investigation into its CEO, Jensen Huang, after he admitted that he was involved in an affair with a business executive who is suspected of being a Chinese spy. Following a New York Times report about Huang's affair with Megaspeed executive and Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang / Huang Le, the Nvidia CEO addressed the situation in a company letter (via the BBC ). "I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry," Huang wrote. "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully." US intelligence believes that Huang was unaware of Alice Huang's alleged activities, and the security branch reportedly has surveillance of her feeding intel to Beijing. The Nvidia board says Huang will remain CEO while the investigation continues, which will involve independent directors and independent counsel. Nvidia added that it doesn't believe the affair compromised any national security or Nvidia secrets. Nvidia has been a giant in the video game space for decades, but in recent years, the graphics card manufacturer has evolved into one of the most important links in the US's artificial intelligence chain. The company has profited massively from the growing AI sector, which has driven the prices of vital components to skyrocket. This has had a knock-on effect on gaming hardware like graphics cards and consoles, which in turn have seen prices hit record highs due to rising memory costs. At the same time, the US under the Trump administration has introduced several new policies to limit China's access to those vital components, with Nvidia emerging as one of the biggest players in the AI arms race. Following the US midterm elections last week, Nvidia's market cap was reduced by more than $1 trillion, although it did start to…

Emphasis on the "little" – it doesn't appear to have gotten very far, despite recently unearthed allusions to "Tokyo PS2" in GTA 5 's source code. Read more

title: 2026’s Games You Should Play Before The Game Awards, Described In One Sentence
description: As is always the case, there is no shortage of great games to play. That can make picking your favorites--or voting for categories in something like The Game Awards--a challenge. With this year's awards just about a month away, we're reflecting on what games we've loved this year to offer up some quick suggestions on what you should consider playing before casting your votes. Below, we've rounded up one-sentence recommendations from our staff. Our goal here was twofold: recognize the games we're individually considering for Game of the Year, whether or not they're well-known, and also spotlight some of the smaller games we loved that you might have missed or never even heard of. Mark Delaney Retro Rewind: Video Store Simulator Retro Rewind Platforms: PC My favorite of all job sims is this one about running a video rental store in the '90s, and it just got a huge update that adds video games to your inventory. See at Steam Big Walk Platforms: PC, PS5, Switch 2 Bring 1-11 buddies on a hefty hike across a puzzle-filled island primed to make lasting memories. See at Steam Control Resonant Platforms: PC, Xbox Series X|S, PS5 What if Remedy took the reins from Sucker Punch and made a new Infamous, complete with the Finnish studio's unique brand of weird? See at Steam Far Far West (early access) Platforms: PC Take the exciting core of Helldivers 2, but put it in a Western with all the cartoonish whimsy you'd expect from the team behind Pumpkin Jack. See at Fanatical Marathon Platforms: PC, Xbox Series X|S, PS5 Bungie's suspenseful extraction shooter feels so damn good--this is Bungie, after all--but its art direction and worldbuilding ensure it looks even better. See at Steam Jessica Cogswell Fields of Mistria Fields of Mistria Platforms: PC I've argued--repeatedly--that Fields of Mistria is the greatest farming life-sim of all-time, surpassing even Stardew Valley, thanks to its '80s to '90s shōjo anime-inspired art direction, blush-inducing romances, and overall gameplay…
